In the second section on the "Single Category" within the second chapter on the Aggregates of Fetters (Saṃyojana-skandha), part two: If one is bound by the fetter of ignorance (avidyā-saṃyojana) regarding a certain object, is one also bound by the fetter of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana) regarding that same object?
Answer: If there is a bond of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana) regarding this object, there must necessarily be a bond of ignorance (avidyā-saṃyojana).
However, there may be a bond of ignorance without a bond of views.
That is to say:
when the knowledge of origination has arisen but the knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen;

regarding those phenomena associated with the fetters of views to be abandoned by the vision of cessation and the path, as well as regarding those phenomena to be abandoned by cultivation, the fetter of ignorance remains unsevered.
When the knowledge of cessation has already arisen, but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen:

regarding those factors dissociated from the fetter of views to be abandoned by the path of seeing, as well as regarding those factors to be abandoned by cultivation, the fetter of ignorance remains unabandoned.
Regarding the disciples of the World-Honored One who possess right view:
with respect to the dharmas to be abandoned through cultivation, there remains the fetter of ignorance that has not yet been severed.
This is the same as in the case of the fetter of views.
The same applies to the fetter of doubt!
If one is bound by the fetter of ignorance regarding a certain object, is one also bound by the fetter of grasping?
Answer:
If there is bondage by the fetter of grasping (upādāna-saṃyojana) regarding this object, there is necessarily bondage by the fetter of ignorance (avidyā-saṃyojana).
However, there may be bondage by the fetter of ignorance without there being bondage by the fetter of grasping.
That is to say:
When the knowledge of origination has arisen but the knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen—regarding phenomena to be abandoned by cultivation, the fetter of ignorance has not been severed.
When the knowledge of cessation has arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen—regarding phenomena to be abandoned by cultivation, the fetter of ignorance has not been severed.

Regarding a disciple of the Blessed One who possesses right view: if there is a fetter of ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*) that has not yet been abandoned with respect to the factors to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya-dharma*), and if this person is bound to this object by the fetter of ignorance, are they also bound to it by the fetter of envy (*īrṣyā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If there is the fetter of envy (īrṣyā-saṃyojana) bound to this object, there is necessarily the fetter of ignorance (avidyā-saṃyojana).
However, there may be the fetter of ignorance bound to it without the fetter of envy.
That is to say:
regarding the phenomena of the desire realm to be abandoned by insight, as well as the phenomena of the form and formless realms, there exists the fetter of ignorance that has not yet been severed;
this is just as it is with the fetter of envy.
The same applies to the fetter of stinginess (*mātsarya-saṃyojana*).
If there is bondage by the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) regarding a certain object, is there also bondage by the fetter of grasping (*parigraha-saṃyojana*)? Answer:
If there is bondage by the fetter of views regarding this object, there is necessarily bondage by the fetter of grasping.
However, there may be bondage by the fetter of grasping without there being bondage by the fetter of views.
That is to say:

When the knowledge of origination has arisen but the knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen—regarding those factors dissociated from the fetter of views to be abandoned by the vision of cessation and the path, the fetter of grasping remains unsevered.

When the knowledge of cessation has arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen—regarding those factors dissociated from the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) which are to be abandoned by the vision of the path, the fetter of grasping (*parāmarśa-saṃyojana*) is not yet abandoned.
If there is a binding by the fetter of views regarding this object, is there also a binding by the fetter of doubt (*vicikitsā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: This should be treated as four propositions (catuṣkoṭi).
There may be one who is bound by the fetter of views (dṛṣṭisaṃyojana) but not bound by the fetter of doubt (vicikitsāsaṃyojana).
That is to say:

when the knowledge of origination has arisen but the knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen—there is as yet no abandonment of the fetter of views regarding those phenomena associated with the fetter of views that are to be abandoned through the vision of cessation and the path.

When the knowledge of cessation has arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen—regarding those phenomena associated with the fetters of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) to be abandoned by the vision of the path, there is the fetter of views that has not yet been abandoned.
Alternatively, there may be the binding of the fetter of doubt (*vicikitsā-saṃyojana*), but no binding of the fetter of views.
That is to say:

when the knowledge of origination has arisen but the knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen—there is the fetter of doubt that has not been abandoned regarding those factors associated with the fetter of doubt that are to be abandoned by the vision of cessation and the path.

When the knowledge of cessation has arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen—regarding those phenomena associated with the fetter of doubt that are to be abandoned by the vision of the path, there is the fetter of doubt that has not been severed;
or, in some cases, both [fetters] bind them.
That is to say:
one who possesses fetters has two fetters binding them with respect to phenomena abandoned through seeing and cultivation.

When the knowledge of suffering has arisen but the knowledge of origin has not yet arisen, they have two fetters binding them with respect to phenomena abandoned through seeing suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those abandoned through cultivation.
Or there may be cases where neither of the two fetters is bound.
That is to say:

when the knowledge of origination has arisen but the knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen—one is not bound by the two fetters regarding those phenomena abandoned through the vision of suffering and origination, nor regarding those phenomena dissociated from the single fetter of views and doubt abandoned through the vision of cessation and the path, nor regarding those phenomena abandoned through cultivation.

When the knowledge of cessation has arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen—regarding those phenomena to be abandoned by the vision of suffering, origin, and cessation, as well as those phenomena dissociated from the two fetters of views and doubt to be abandoned by the vision of the path, and furthermore regarding those phenomena to be abandoned by cultivation—there is no bondage by these two fetters.
A disciple of the World-Honored One who possesses right view has no two fetters binding them regarding phenomena to be abandoned through seeing and cultivation.
One who is already free from the defilement of desire has no two fetters binding them regarding phenomena of the desire realm.
Having already become free from the defilement of form—one has no bonds of the two fetters regarding phenomena of the desire and form realms.
Having already become free from the defilement of the formless—one has no bonds of the two fetters regarding phenomena of the three realms.
If there is a binding by the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) regarding this object, is there also a binding by the fetter of envy (*īrṣyā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: One should formulate four alternatives (*catuṣkoṭika*).
There may be one who is bound by the fetter of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana) but not bound by the fetter of envy (īrṣyā-saṃyojana).

This refers to one for whom the fetter of views regarding the factors to be abandoned by insight (darśana-prahātavya-dharma) within the desire realm, as well as those factors of the form and formless realms, has not yet been abandoned.
There may be one who is bound by the fetter of envy (*īrṣyā-saṃyojana*) but not bound by the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*).

This refers to one who has not yet abandoned the defilement of desire (*kāmarāga*), for whom the knowledge of origination (*samudaya-jñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-jñāna*) has not yet arisen; such a person has not yet abandoned the fetter of envy regarding those phenomena of the desire realm to be abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).

When the knowledge of cessation has arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen—there is the fetter of envy that has not been abandoned regarding the factors of the desire realm to be abandoned by cultivation.

For a disciple of the Blessed One who possesses vision but has not yet become free from the defilement of desire—there is the fetter of envy that has not been abandoned regarding the factors of the desire realm to be abandoned by cultivation.
Or there may be those bound by both:
that is, one who is fully fettered has two types of fetters regarding the dharmas of the desire realm to be abandoned through cultivation.

For one who has not yet abandoned the defilement of sensual desire, when the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen—there are two fetters (*saṃyojana*) binding them to the phenomena of the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*) to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).
Alternatively, there may be cases where they are bound by neither of the two.
That is to say:

for one who has not yet abandoned the defilement of desire—when the knowledge of origination (*samudaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-jñāna*) has not yet arisen—there is no bondage by two fetters (*saṃyojana*) with respect to those phenomena abandoned through the vision of suffering and origination, nor with respect to those phenomena dissociated from the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) abandoned through the vision of cessation and the path, nor with respect to the phenomena abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*) belonging to the form and formless realms.

When the knowledge of cessation has already arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen—one is bound by neither of the two fetters with respect to those phenomena abandoned through the vision of suffering, origin, and cessation; nor with respect to those phenomena associated with the fetter of views abandoned through the vision of the path; nor with respect to those phenomena abandoned through cultivation in the form and formless realms.

A disciple of the Blessed One who possesses right view, but has not yet abandoned the defilements of desire, is bound by no more than two fetters regarding the factors to be abandoned by seeing, as well as the factors to be abandoned by cultivation pertaining to the realms of form and formlessness.
Having already become free from the defilement of desire—one has no bonds of the two fetters regarding phenomena of the desire realm.
Having already become free from the defilement of form—one has no bonds of the two fetters regarding phenomena of the desire and form realms.
Having already become detached from the defilements of the formless realm— one is not bound by the two fetters toward any phenomena of the three realms.
As it is with the fetter of envy,
so it is with the fetter of avarice.
Just as the fetter of attachment (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) forms one category following its respective counterparts, so too does the fetter of doubt (*vicikitsā-saṃyojana*).
If there is the binding of the fetter of attachment with respect to a certain object, is there also the binding of the fetter of doubt?
Answer: If one is bound by the fetter of doubt (*vicikitsā-saṃyojana*) with respect to a certain object, one is necessarily bound by the fetter of grasping (*parigraha-saṃyojana*).
However, there may be cases where one is bound by the fetter of grasping without being bound by the fetter of doubt.
That is to say:

when the knowledge of origination has arisen but the knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen—there is the fetter of grasping (*parāmarśa-saṃyojana*) that has not been abandoned regarding those phenomena dissociated from the fetter of doubt (*vicikitsā-saṃyojana*) which are to be abandoned through the vision of cessation and the path.

When the knowledge of cessation has arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen—regarding those phenomena dissociated from the fetter of doubt that are to be abandoned by the vision of the path, the fetter of grasping (*parāmarśa*) is not yet abandoned.
If, with respect to these phenomena, there is the bondage of the fetter of grasping, is there also the bondage of the fetter of envy (*īrṣyā*)?
Answer: This should be treated as four propositions (catuṣkoṭi).
There may be cases where one is bound by the fetter of grasping (parāmarśa-saṃyojana), but not bound by the fetter of envy (īrṣyā-saṃyojana).
That is to say:
regarding the factors abandoned through vision in the desire realm, as well as the factors of the form and formless realms, there is the fetter of grasping that has not yet been abandoned;
or else, there is the bond of the fetter of envy, but no bond of the fetter of grasping.
That is to say:

for one who has not yet abandoned the defilement of desire—having already produced the knowledge of origination (*samudaya-jñāna*) but not yet produced the knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-jñāna*)—there remains the fetter of envy (*īrṣyā-saṃyojana*) that has not been abandoned regarding the factors of the desire realm to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).
When the knowledge of cessation has arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen— one who is a disciple of the World-Honored One possessed of vision,
yet not free from the defilement of desire— there remains the fetter of envy regarding those phenomena of the desire realm to be abandoned by cultivation that have not yet been abandoned.
Or there may be cases where both are bound;
that is to say,
for one who is fully fettered (sakalabandhana), there are two fetters (saṃyojana) binding them to the dharmas of the desire realm abandoned through cultivation (bhāvanā-heya).

For one who has not yet abandoned the defilements of desire, when the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen—regarding the phenomena of the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*) to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*)—there are two fetters (*saṃyojana*) that bind;
or, in some cases, there may be none bound by either.
That is to say:

for one who has not yet abandoned the defilement of desire—having already produced the knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) but not yet produced the knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-jñāna*)—there is no bondage by the two fetters (*saṃyojana*) with respect to those phenomena abandoned through the vision of suffering and origin, as well as those phenomena of the form and formless realms abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).

When the knowledge of cessation has arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen—one is bound by neither of the two fetters with respect to those phenomena abandoned through the vision of suffering, origin, and cessation, nor with respect to those phenomena of the form and formless realms abandoned through cultivation.

A disciple of the Blessed One who possesses right view, though not yet free from the taints of desire, has no two fetters binding them with respect to the factors abandoned by vision, nor with respect to the factors abandoned by cultivation in the realms of form and formlessness.
Having already become free from the defilement of desire—one has no bondage by the two fetters regarding phenomena of the desire realm.
Having already become free from the defilement of form—one has no bondage by the two fetters regarding phenomena of the desire and form realms.
Having already become free from the defilements of the formless realm— one has no two fetters binding one to the phenomena of the three realms.
As it is with the fetter of envy,
so it is with the fetter of avarice.
If one is bound to this object by the fetter of envy (*īrṣyā-saṃyojana*), is one also bound by the fetter of stinginess (*mātsarya-saṃyojana*)? Answer: It is so.
If there is the fetter of stinginess (mātsarya-saṃyojana), is there also the fetter of envy (īrṣyā-saṃyojana)? Answer: It is so.
If there is a bond of past craving regarding this object, is there also one of the future? Answer: It is so.
If there is that which is future, is there also that which is past? Answer:
If what was previously produced has not been severed, then one is bound.
If it has not yet arisen previously, or if it has arisen and been abandoned, then one is not bound by it.
If one is bound to this object by a past fetter of craving, is one also bound by a present one?
Answer: If it is present, does it also have a past?
Answer: If it has arisen previously and has not been abandoned, one is bound by it;
if it has not arisen previously, or if having arisen it has been abandoned, one is not bound by it.
If there is a bond of future craving (anāgata-tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana) regarding this object, is there also one of the present?
Answer: If it is present before one.
If there is the present, is there also the future? Answer: It is so.
If there is a bond of past craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) regarding this object, is there also [a bond] of the future and the present?
Answer: There is necessarily a bond of the future; as for the present, it exists if it is manifest at the present moment.
If there are future and present [fetters], are there also past ones?
Answer: If they were previously produced and have not yet been abandoned, then one is bound by them.
If it has not yet arisen previously, or if it has arisen and been subsequently severed, then one is not bound by it.
If there is a future fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) bound to this object, is there also [a fetter of craving] in the past and present?
Answer: There may be that which exists in the future, but not in the past or the present.
That is to say:
Regarding this matter, the fetter of craving has not been abandoned; yet it has not arisen previously, or if it has arisen, it has been abandoned and does not manifest in the present.
There may be [craving] in the future and the past, but none in the present.
That is to say:
regarding this object, there is a fetter of craving that arose previously and has not been abandoned, though it is not currently manifest;
or else, it exists either in the future or in the present.
There is no past [bond].
That is to say:
regarding this object, the fetter of craving (anunaya-saṃyojana) is present, yet it has not previously arisen, or, having arisen, it has already been abandoned.
There may be [fetters] belonging to the future, the past, and the present;
that is to say:
regarding this object, the fetter of craving has not been abandoned in a previous life and is also manifest at present.
If there are past and present [phenomena], are there also future ones? Answer: It is so.
If there is a bond of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) for this object in the present, is there also [a bond] in the past and future?
Answer: There is necessarily a bond in the future.
If [the defilement] was not severed in the past or in a previous life, then one is bound by it;
if it had not yet arisen in the past, or if it arose but has since been severed, then one is not bound by it.
If there is the past and the future, is there also the present?
Answer: If it is present before one,

just as the fetter of craving (rāga-saṃyojana) passes through the six [realms], one should know that the fetters of aversion (pratigha), pride (māna), envy (īrṣyā), stinginess (mātsarya), and non-universal ignorance (asarvatraga-avidyā) likewise pass through the six in the same manner.
If, regarding this matter, there is bondage by the fetter of views (dṛṣṭisaṃyojana) in the past, is there also [bondage] in the future? Answer: It is so.
If there is a future, is there also a past? Answer: It is so.
If, regarding this object, there is bondage by the fetter of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana) in the past, is there also [bondage] in the present?
Answer: If it is present before one.
If there is the present, is there also the past? Answer: It is so.
If there is a future fetter of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana) bound to this object, is there also one that is present?
Answer: If it is manifested in the present.
If there is the present, is there also the future? Answer: It is so.
If, regarding this object, there is bondage by the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) in the past, is there also [bondage] in the future and the present?
Answer: There is necessarily bondage in the future; as for the present, it depends on whether [the fetter] is currently manifest.
If there are future and present [dharmas], are there also past ones? Answer: Yes.
If, regarding this object, there is a bond of future views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*), is there also [a bond] of the past and the present?
Answer: There is necessarily a bond of the past; as for the present, it exists if it is currently manifest.
If there are past and present [dharmas], are there also future ones? Answer: It is so.
If, regarding this matter, there is bondage by the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭisaṃyojana*) in the present, is there also [bondage] in the past and the future? Answer: It is so.
If there are past and future [dharmas], are there also present ones?
Answer: If they are manifest before one.

Just as the fetter of attachment (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) traverses six [objects], one should know that the fetters of grasping (*parāmarśa*), doubt (*vicikitsā*), and pervasive ignorance (*sarvatraga-avidyā-saṃyojana*) likewise traverse six.
If there is a past bond of the fetter of attachment toward this object, is there also a past bond of the fetter of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If it has arisen previously and has not been abandoned, then one is bound;
if it has not arisen previously, or if it arose but has already been abandoned, then one is not bound.
If there is a past fetter of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*), is there also a past fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If it was previously produced and not yet abandoned, then one is bound by it.
If it has not yet arisen previously, or if it has arisen and been abandoned, then one is not bound by it.
If one is bound to this object by the past fetter of craving, is one also bound to it by the future fetter of aversion?
Answer: If it has not been abandoned,
and there is the future fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*), is there also the past fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If that which arose previously has not been abandoned, then one is bound;
if it had not arisen previously, or if having arisen it has been abandoned, then one is not bound.
If there is a bond of past craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) regarding this object, is there also a bond of present aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If it is presently manifest.
If there is a present fetter of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*), is there also a past fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If it was previously produced and not yet abandoned, then one is bound by it.
If it has not previously arisen, or if having arisen it has been abandoned, then one is not bound by it.
If one is bound to this object by the past fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*), is one also bound to it by the past or present fetter of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*)?
Answer:
There may be one who is bound by the fetter of past craving, but is not bound by the fetters of past or present aversion.
That is to say:
In this matter, there is the fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) that arose previously and has not yet been abandoned;
there is no fetter of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) that arose previously, and even if it had arisen, it has been abandoned and does not manifest.
Alternatively, there may be the past binding of the fetter of craving as well as the past binding of the fetter of aversion, but none in the present.
That is to say:

regarding this object, there are the fetters of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) and hostility (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) that arose previously and have not yet been abandoned, but the fetter of hostility is not currently manifest.
Or, there may be the past bond of the fetter of craving as well as the present bond of the fetter of hostility, but no past [bond].
That is to say:
regarding this object, there is a previously arisen fetter of craving that has not yet been abandoned,
and a fetter of aversion is currently manifest.
Yet it has not previously arisen;
or, even if it has arisen, it has been abandoned.
Alternatively, there may be bondage by the past fetter of craving, as well as bondage by the past and present fetters of aversion.
That is to say:

regarding this object, there are the fetters of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) and hostility (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) that arose previously and have not yet been abandoned, and furthermore, the fetter of hostility is present.
If one is bound by past and present fetters of hostility, is one also bound by past fetters of craving?
Answer: If it has previously arisen and has not been abandoned, then one is bound;
if it has not previously arisen, or if having arisen it has already been abandoned, then one is not bound.
If there is a bond of past attachment (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) regarding this object, is there also a bond of future or present aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: There may be a bond of past attachment, yet no bond of future or present aversion.
That is to say:
regarding phenomena of the form and formless realms, there is a previously arisen craving-fetter (*rāga-saṃyojana*) that has not yet been abandoned;
or there is a past craving-fetter with which one is bound, as well as a future aversion-fetter (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) with which one is bound, but none that are present.
That is to say:

regarding this object, there is a previously arisen fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) that has not yet been abandoned, as well as a fetter of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) that has not yet been abandoned, though it is not currently manifest.
Alternatively, there may be a past fetter of craving binding [the mind], while there is also a future and present fetter of aversion binding it.
That is to say:
regarding this object, there is a previously arisen fetter of craving that has not yet been abandoned,
and a fetter of aversion is currently manifest.
If there is bondage by the future and present fetters of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*), is there also bondage by the past fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If it was previously produced and not yet abandoned, then there is bondage.
If it has not yet arisen previously, or if having arisen it has been severed, then one is not bound by it.
If one is bound to this object by the past fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*), is one also bound to it by the past and future fetters of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: There may be one who is bound by the fetter of attachment (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) in the past, but is not bound by the fetter of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) in the past or future.
That is to say:
Regarding phenomena of the form and formless realms, there is a previously arisen craving-fetter (*rāga-saṃyojana*) that has not yet been abandoned.
Alternatively, there may be a past craving-fetter and a future aversion-fetter (*pratigha-saṃyojana*), but no past one.
That is to say:

regarding this object, there is a previously arisen fetter of attachment that has not yet been abandoned, as well as a fetter of aversion that has not yet been abandoned; however, there is no previously arisen fetter of aversion, or if one arose, it has already been abandoned.
There may be one who is bound by the fetter of attachment (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) in the past, and also bound by the fetter of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) in both the past and the future.
That is to say:
regarding this object, the fetter of attachment and the fetter of aversion have arisen previously and have not yet been abandoned.
If there is bondage by the past and future fetters of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*), is there also bondage by the past fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If it was previously produced and not yet abandoned, then there is bondage.
If it has not yet arisen previously, or if having arisen it has been severed, then one is not bound by it.
If one is bound to this object by the past fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*), is one also bound to it by the past, future, or present fetter of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: There may be one who is bound by the fetter of attachment (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) in the past, but is not bound by the fetter of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) in the past, future, or present.
That is to say:
Regarding phenomena of the form and formless realms, there is a previously arisen craving-fetter (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) that has not yet been abandoned.
Alternatively, there may be a past craving-fetter binding [the mind], as well as a future hatred-fetter (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) binding it, but no past or present [fetters].
That is to say:

regarding this object, there is a previously arisen *anunaya-saṃyojana* (fetter of attachment) that has not yet been abandoned; and there is a *pratigha-saṃyojana* (fetter of aversion) that has not yet been abandoned and has not yet arisen, even if it had arisen previously, it has been abandoned and does not manifest at present.

There may be one who is bound by the fetter of attachment (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) in the past, and bound by the fetter of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) in both the future and the present, but not in the past.

This refers to a case where, regarding a particular object, the fetter of attachment arose previously and has not yet been abandoned, while the fetter of aversion is currently manifest but had not arisen before; or, even if it had arisen, it has already been abandoned.

There may be one who is bound by the fetter of attachment (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) of the past, as well as bound by the fetters of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) of the past and future, but not of the present.
That is to say:
regarding this object, the fetters of attachment and aversion have arisen previously and have not yet been abandoned, yet the fetter of aversion is not currently manifest.
There may be one who is bound by the fetter of attachment (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) in the past, and is also bound by the fetters of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) in the past, future, and present.
That is to say:
regarding this object, there is a previously arisen attachment-fetter and aversion-fetter that have not yet been abandoned, and furthermore, an aversion-fetter is currently manifest.
If there is a bond of resentment (pratigha-saṃyojana) belonging to the past, future, or present, is there also a bond of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana) belonging to the past?
Answer: If it was previously produced and not yet abandoned, then one is bound.
If [the fetter] has not previously arisen, or if it has arisen and been abandoned, then one is not bound by it.
As with the fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*),
so it is also with the fetters of envy (*īrṣyā-saṃyojana*) and avarice (*mātsarya-saṃyojana*).
As for the distinctions:

regarding the factors abandoned through vision (*darśana-prahātavya*) in the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*), as well as the factors of the form and formless realms (*rūpa-ārūpyadhātu*), there is the fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) that has arisen previously and remains unsevered; however, there is no past, future, or present fetter of envy (*īrṣyā-saṃyojana*) or avarice (*mātsarya-saṃyojana*).
If there is bondage by the past fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) regarding this object, is there also bondage by the past fetter of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If it was previously produced and has not been abandoned, then there is bondage.
If it has not yet arisen previously, or if having arisen it has been abandoned, then one is not bound by it.
Suppose there is a past fetter of conceit (māna-saṃyojana) binding one; is there also a past fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana) binding one?
Answer: If it has arisen previously and has not been abandoned, then one is bound;
if it has not arisen previously, or if it arose but has already been abandoned, then one is not bound.
If, regarding this matter, there is bondage by the past fetter of craving, is there also bondage by the future fetter of conceit? Answer: It is so.
If there is a future fetter of conceit (*māna*), is there also a past fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā*)?
Answer: If it was previously produced and not yet abandoned, then one is bound by it.
If it has not yet arisen previously, or if having arisen it has already been abandoned, then one is not bound by it.
If one is bound to this object by the past fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*), is one also bound to it by the present fetter of pride (*māna-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If it is present before one,
and there is the bond of the present conceit-fetter (*māna-saṃyojana*), is there also the bond of the past craving-fetter (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If it has arisen previously and has not been abandoned, then one is bound;
if it has not arisen previously, or if it arose but has already been abandoned, then one is not bound.
If, regarding this matter, there is bondage by the past fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*), is there also bondage by the past and present fetters of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: There may be bondage by the past fetter of craving, yet no bondage by the past or present fetters of conceit.
That is to say:

regarding this object, there is a previously arisen love-fetter (*rāga-saṃyojana*) that has not yet been abandoned; there is no previously arisen conceit-fetter (*māna-saṃyojana*), or if it did arise, it has already been abandoned and does not manifest.
Alternatively, there may be a past love-fetter binding [the mind], as well as a past conceit-fetter binding [the mind], but none that are present.

regarding this object, the fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) and the fetter of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*) have previously arisen and have not yet been abandoned;

There may be one who is bound by the fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) in the past and also bound by the fetter of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*) in the present, but not in the past.

regarding this particular object, the fetter of craving arose previously and has not yet been abandoned.

it has not arisen previously;

There may be one who is bound by the fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) of the past, and also bound by the fetter of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*) of the past and present.

regarding this object, the fetter of craving and the fetter of conceit have arisen previously and have not yet been abandoned, and furthermore, the fetter of conceit is currently manifest.
If there is bondage by the fetter of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*) belonging to the past and present, is there also bondage by the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) belonging to the past?
Answer: If it was not abandoned in a previous life, then there is bondage.
If it has not yet arisen previously, or if having arisen it has been severed, then one is not bound by it.
If one is bound to this object by the past fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*), is one also bound to it by the future and present fetters of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: It is necessarily bound in the future, and if it is present, it is bound when it manifests before one.
If there is binding by the fetter of conceit (māna-saṃyojana) in the future and the present, is there also binding by the fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana) in the past?
Answer: If it has arisen previously and has not been abandoned, then one is bound;
if it has not arisen previously, or if it arose but has already been abandoned, then one is not bound.
If there is a bond of past craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) regarding this object, is there also a bond of past and future conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: There is necessarily a bond of the future.
If past [conceit] was not severed in a previous life, then one is bound by it;
if it had not yet arisen previously, or if it arose but was subsequently severed, then one is not bound by it.
If there is bondage by the fetter of past and future conceit, is there also bondage by the fetter of past craving?
Answer: If it has previously arisen and has not been abandoned, then one is bound;
if it has not previously arisen, or if it arose but has already been abandoned, then one is not bound.
If, regarding this object, there is bondage by the past fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*), is there also bondage by the past, future, and present fetters of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*)?
Answer:
There may be bondage by the past fetter of craving and bondage by the future fetter of conceit, but not by the past or present [fetters of conceit].

regarding this object, there is a previously arisen fetter of craving that has not yet been abandoned,

Alternatively, there may be the past fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*), as well as the past and future fetters of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*), but none that are present.

regarding this object, there is a previously arisen *anuśaya* of craving (*rāga*) and a previously arisen *anuśaya* of pride (*māna*) that have not yet been abandoned, but no *anuśaya* of pride is currently manifest.

If there is a fetter of conceit (māna-saṃyojana) bound to the past, future, and present, is there also a fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana) bound to the past?

If one is bound to this object by the past fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*), is one also bound to it by the past fetter of ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: It is so.
If there is a past fetter of ignorance, is there also a past fetter of craving?
Answer: If it has arisen previously and has not been abandoned, then one is bound;
if it has not arisen previously, or if having arisen it has already been abandoned, then one is not bound.
If there is a bond of past craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) regarding this object, is there also a bond of future ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*)? Answer: It is so.
If there is the fetter of ignorance bound in the future, is there also the fetter of craving bound in the past?
Answer: If it was not severed in a previous life, then one is bound.
If it has not yet arisen previously, or if having arisen it has been severed, then one is not bound.
If one is bound by the past fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) regarding this object, is one also bound by the present fetter of ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If it is present before one,
and there is the bond of the fetter of ignorance (avidyā-saṃyojana) in the present, is there also the bond of the fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana) in the past?
Answer: If that which arose previously has not been severed, then one is bound;
if it did not arise previously, or if it arose but has since been severed, then one is not bound.
If there is bondage by the past fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) regarding this object, is there also bondage by the past and present fetters of ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: There is necessarily bondage by the past; as for the present, it depends on whether [the ignorance] is currently manifest.
If there is a bond of past and present ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*),
is there also a bond of past craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*)? Answer:
If it was previously produced and not yet abandoned, then one is bound;
if it was not previously produced, or if having been produced it has already been abandoned, then one is not bound.
If one is bound by the past fetter of craving regarding this object, is one also bound by the future and present fetters of ignorance?
Answer: It is necessarily bound in the future; as for the present, it is so if it is currently manifest.
If there is bondage by the fetter of ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*) in the future and present, is there also bondage by the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) in the past?
Answer: If it has arisen previously and has not been abandoned, then one is bound;
if it has not arisen previously, or if it arose but has already been abandoned, then one is not bound.
If, regarding this object, there is bondage by the past fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*), is there also bondage by the past and future fetters of ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*)? Answer: It is so.
If there is a bond of past and future ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*), is there also a bond of past craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If it was not severed in a previous life, then one is bound.
If it has not yet arisen previously, or if having arisen it has been severed, then one is not bound by it.
If one is bound to this object by the past fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*), is one also bound to it by the past, future, and present fetters of ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: Those of the past and future are necessarily bound; those of the present are bound if they are currently manifest.
If there is bondage by the fetter of ignorance (avidyā-saṃyojana) of the past, future, or present, is there also bondage by the fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana) of the past?
Answer: If that which arose previously has not been severed, then one is bound;
if it did not arise previously, or if it arose but has already been severed, then one is not bound.
If there is a bond of past craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) regarding this object, is there also a bond of past views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If it has not been abandoned.
If there is bondage by the past fetter of views, is there also bondage by the past fetter of craving?
Answer: If it was not abandoned in a previous life, then there is bondage.
If it has not yet arisen previously, or if it has arisen and been abandoned, then one is not bound by it.
If one is bound to this object by the past fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*), is one also bound to it by the future fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If it has not been abandoned,
and there is a future fetter of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana), is there also a past fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana)?
Answer: If it has arisen previously and has not been abandoned, then one is bound;
if it has not arisen previously, or if it arose but has already been abandoned, then one is not bound.
If there is bondage by the past fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) regarding this object, is there also bondage by the present fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If it is present before one.
If there is a present fetter of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana), is there also a past fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana)?
Answer: If it was not abandoned in a previous life, then one is bound by it.
If it has not yet arisen previously, or if it has arisen and been abandoned, then one is not bound by it.
If one is bound to this object by the past fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*), is one also bound to it by the past and present fetters of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*)?

Regarding this matter, there may be a previously arisen fetter of craving that has not yet been abandoned, while the fetter of views has already been abandoned.

Or, there may be a past craving-fetter binding it, as well as past and present view-fetters binding it.

regarding this object, there is a craving-fetter (*rāga-saṃyojana*) that arose previously and has not yet been abandoned, and there is also a view-fetter (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) that is currently present.
If there is a past or present view-fetter binding [this object], is there also a past craving-fetter binding it?
Answer: If that which arose previously has not been severed, then one is bound;
if it did not arise previously, or if having arisen it has been severed, then one is not bound.
If, regarding this matter, there is bondage by the past fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*), is there also bondage by the future and present fetters of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: There may be bondage by the past fetter of craving, without there being bondage by the future or present fetters of views.

regarding this object, the fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) has arisen previously and remains unsevered,
whereas the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) has already been severed.
There may be one who is bound by the fetter of craving in the past and bound by the fetter of views in the future, but not in the present.

Regarding this matter, there is a previously arisen fetter of craving that has not yet been abandoned,
as well as a fetter of views that has not yet been abandoned,
yet they do not manifest at present.
There may be one who is bound by the fetter of craving (anunaya-saṃyojana) in the past, and also bound by the fetter of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana) in the future and the present.
That is to say:
regarding this particular object, there was craving that arose previously and has not yet been abandoned.
Furthermore, when the fetter of views (dṛṣṭisaṃyojana) is present,
if there is a future or present bondage by the fetter of views,
is there also a past bondage by the fetter of craving (tṛṣṇāsaṃyojana)?
Answer: If it arose previously and has not been abandoned, then one is bound by it.
If it has not yet arisen, or if having arisen it has been abandoned, then one is not bound by it.
If one is bound to this object by past fetters of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*), is one also bound to it by past and future fetters of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If it has not been abandoned,
there is the bondage of the fetter of views (dṛṣṭisaṃyojana) regarding the past and the future.
Furthermore, is there also bondage by the fetter of craving for the past? Answer:
If it was previously produced and not yet abandoned, then one is bound.
If it has not yet arisen previously, or if it has arisen and been abandoned, then one is not bound by it.
If one is bound to this object by the past fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*), is one also bound to it by the past, future, and present fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*)?
Answer:

That is to say:
In this matter, there is the fetter of craving (rāga-saṃyojana) that arose previously and has not yet been abandoned,
while the fetter of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana) has already been abandoned;
or else, there is the past fetter of craving that still binds.
Furthermore, there may be bondage by the fetter of views regarding the past and future, but none regarding the present. This refers to a case where,

there may be the past fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*), as well as the past, future, and present fetters of views.

regarding this object, there is a previously arisen craving-fetter (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) that has not yet been abandoned,
and furthermore, a view-fetter (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) is currently manifest.
If there is bondage by the fetter of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana) pertaining to the past, future, and present,
is there also bondage by the fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana) pertaining to the past? Answer:
If that which arose previously has not been abandoned, one is bound;
if it has not arisen previously, or if having arisen it has been abandoned, one is not bound.
