Roots abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), which have as their object the knowledge of the dharma regarding suffering (*duḥkha-dharmajñāna-prahātavya*). And roots abandoned through the vision of origination (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*), which have as their cause those abandoned through the vision of suffering and as their object the knowledge of the dharma regarding suffering.
Those [roots] which have as their cause those abandoned through the vision of suffering and as their object the knowledge of the dharma regarding origination (*samudaya-dharmajñāna-prahātavya*).
That is to say:

faculties abandoned through the vision of suffering (duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya) which have as their object the knowledge of the dharma regarding origination (samudaya-dharmajñāna-prahātavya); and faculties abandoned through the vision of origination (samudaya-darśana-prahātavya) which have as their cause those abandoned through the vision of suffering and have as their object the knowledge of the dharma regarding origination.
Those abandoned through the vision of suffering, which have as their object the subsequent knowledge of origination:
this refers to faculties abandoned through the vision of suffering that take as their object the subsequent knowledge of origination.

Furthermore, regarding those [factors] that are abandoned by the vision of origination (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*), which have as their cause those [factors] abandoned by the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), and which are abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origination (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*): as for those that have as their cause those [factors] abandoned by the vision of suffering, and are abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-dharma-jñāna*), it is said:
Roots abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), which have as their object the knowledge of the dharma regarding cessation (*nirodha-dharmajñāna-prahātavya*);

and roots abandoned through the vision of origin (*samudaya-darśana*) and the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana*), which have as their cause those abandoned through the vision of suffering and as their object the knowledge of the dharma regarding cessation.
Those abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*) which have as their object the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna-prahātavya*):
this refers to faculties abandoned through the vision of suffering that take as their object what is abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of cessation.

Furthermore, regarding those [factors] abandoned through the vision of origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*) or abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), which have as their cause those abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*) and as their object the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*);
and those which have as their cause those abandoned through the vision of suffering and as their object the dharma-knowledge of the path (*mārga-dharma-jñāna*).
That is to say:
faculties abandoned through the vision of suffering (duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya) which take as their object the knowledge of the dharma regarding the path (mārga-dharmajñāna-prahātavya);

and faculties abandoned through the vision of origin (samudaya-darśana-prahātavya) or the vision of the path (mārga-darśana-prahātavya), which have as their cause those abandoned through the vision of suffering and take as their object the knowledge of the dharma regarding the path.
Those abandoned through the vision of suffering (duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya) which take the subsequent knowledge of the path (mārgānvaya-jñāna) as their object:
this refers to faculties abandoned through the vision of suffering that take the subsequent knowledge of the path as their object.

Furthermore, regarding those [factors] abandoned by the vision of origin (samudaya-darśana-prahātavya) and abandoned by the vision of the path (mārga-darśana-prahātavya), which have as their cause those abandoned by the vision of suffering (duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya) and as their object the abandonment through subsequent knowledge of the path (mārga-anvaya-jñāna-prahātavya): they have as their cause those abandoned by the vision of suffering and as their object those abandoned by cultivation (bhāvanā-prahātavya).
That is to say:

faculties abandoned through the vision of suffering (duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya) which take as their object those things to be abandoned through cultivation (bhāvanā-prahātavya); and faculties abandoned through the vision of origin (samudaya-darśana-prahātavya) or through cultivation, which have as their cause those things abandoned through the vision of suffering and take as their object those things to be abandoned through cultivation.
Regarding those [factors] that are abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*) as causes,

while being non-abandonable as objects (*anālambana*): this refers to the faculties (*indriya*) that are abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*) and the vision of the path (*mārga-darśana-prahātavya*), which have as their cause those factors abandoned through the vision of suffering, while being non-abandonable as objects.
Those abandoned through the vision of suffering that have no object refer to the root-faculties (indriya) that lack an object and are abandoned through the vision of suffering.

If a faculty has suffering-subsequent-knowledge-abandonment (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna-prahātavya*) as its object, does that faculty have suffering-view-abandonment (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*) as its cause? Answer:
Those faculties that have suffering-subsequent-knowledge-abandonment as their object may have suffering-view-abandonment as their cause.
Some are abandoned through the vision of the origin [of suffering], some are abandoned through cultivation,
and some are not abandoned.

Regarding those faculties that have the knowledge of the subsequent realization of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) as their object-condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*) and are abandoned through the vision of suffering (*darśana-heya*):
this refers to faculties that are themselves abandoned through the vision of suffering and take the knowledge of the subsequent realization of suffering as their object-condition.

Furthermore, regarding those factors abandoned by the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*) that have as their cause those factors abandoned by the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*),
and which take as their object those factors abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkhānvaya-jñāna-prahātavya*):
it refers to—

Roots abandoned through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*) that take as their object the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna-prahātavya*); and roots abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*) that have as their cause those abandoned through the vision of the origin and take as their object the subsequent knowledge of suffering;
and those that take as their object the subsequent knowledge of suffering and have as their cause those abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-prahātavya*).
That is to say:

the faculties are abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*), they have as their object that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna-heya*), and they have as their cause that which is not abandoned (*aheya*).
That is to say:
when the faculty is not abandoned, it is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*). As it is with regard to suffering; so it is for the others.
The same applies to origination (*samudaya*).

Regarding those faculties whose cause is abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), are those faculties also abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of cessation (*nirodha-dharmajñāna*)? Answer:
Those faculties that have as their cause the abandonment through the vision of cessation may have as their object the knowledge of the dharma of cessation,
or the subsequent knowledge of cessation,
or the knowledge of cultivation.
Some have non-abandonment as their object; some have no object.
Those faculties whose cause is abandoned through the vision of cessation, and which are abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of cessation—[these are such].
That is to say:

those faculties that are abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodhadarśana-prahātavya*) and take as their object the knowledge of the dharma of cessation (*nirodhadharmajñāna-prahātavya*), and those that are abandoned through the vision of cessation and take as their object the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodhānvayajñāna-prahātavya*).
That is to say:

those faculties that are abandoned through the vision of cessation (nirodha-darśana-prahātavya) and take as their object the knowledge of the category of cessation (nirodha-anvaya-jñāna-prahātavya), which have as their cause that which is abandoned through the vision of cessation and take as their object that which is abandoned through cultivation (bhāvanā-prahātavya).
That is to say:

a faculty that is abandoned through cultivation (bhāvanā-heya), which has as its cause that which is abandoned through the vision of cessation (nirodha-darśana-heya), and which takes as its object that which is abandoned through cultivation; and that which has as its cause that which is abandoned through the vision of cessation, and which takes as its object that which is not abandoned (aheya).
That is to say:

there are faculties that are abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodhadarśana-prahātavya*) and take what is not abandoned as their object; and there are those that are abandoned through the vision of cessation and have no object at all.
That is to say:

if there is a faculty that does not take [the object] as its condition, but which, being caused by what is abandoned through the vision of cessation, takes as its condition a faculty that is abandoned through the knowledge of the cessation of phenomena (*dharmajñāna*), is that faculty caused by what is abandoned through the vision of cessation? Answer: [The root text continues with the formal response.]

Regarding those faculties whose objects are abandoned by the knowledge of the extinction of phenomena (*nirodhadharma-jñāna*), those faculties are either abandoned through the vision of extinction (*nirodha-darśana*),
or abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana*), or abandoned through the vision of origination (*samudaya-darśana*).
Or [the faculties] may be abandoned through cultivation, or not abandoned;
those faculties that have cessation-dharma-knowledge as their object and are abandoned through the vision of cessation.
That is to say:
a faculty that is abandoned through the vision of cessation and takes as its object that which is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of cessation,
while being caused by that which is abandoned through the vision of suffering.
That is to say:
faculties abandoned through the vision of suffering (duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya) which take as their object the knowledge of the dharma of cessation (nirodha-dharmajñāna-prahātavya);

and faculties abandoned through the vision of origin (samudaya-darśana-prahātavya) or the vision of cessation (nirodha-darśana-prahātavya), which have as their cause those abandoned through the vision of suffering and take as their object the knowledge of the dharma of cessation.
Those that have cessation through the knowledge of the dharma as their object-condition and are abandoned by the vision of the origin as their cause refer to:
faculties abandoned by the vision of the origin, which have cessation through the knowledge of the dharma as their object-condition.

Furthermore, regarding those faculties abandoned through the vision of suffering and the vision of cessation, which have as their cause what is abandoned through the vision of origination, and as their object what is abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of cessation:
that which has as its object what is abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of cessation, yet has as its cause what is abandoned through cultivation.
That is to say:

when the faculties are to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*), they take as their object that which is to be abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of cessation (*nirodha-dharma-jñāna-heya*); and when taking as their object that which is to be abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of cessation, they have as their cause that which is not to be abandoned (*aheya*).
That is to say:

if the faculties are not abandoned by means of the knowledge of the cessation of phenomena (*dharmajñāna*), but are abandoned by means of the knowledge of the cessation [of suffering] (*nirodhajñāna*), then are those faculties, which have as their cause the vision of the cessation [of suffering], also abandoned by means of the subsequent knowledge of the cessation (*nirodhānvayajñāna*)?

Answer: Those faculties whose causes are to be abandoned through the vision of cessation may have as their object either that which is to be abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*) or that which is to be abandoned through the dharma-knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-dharma-jñāna*).
Some take as their object that which is abandoned through cultivation; some take as their object that which is not abandoned;
and some have no object.

Those faculties that have as their cause what is abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodhadarśana-prahātavya*), and have as their object what is abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodhānvaya-jñāna-prahātavya*): this refers to those faculties that are themselves abandoned through the vision of cessation, and have as their object what is abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of cessation.
Regarding those abandoned through the vision of cessation and those abandoned through the dharma-knowledge of cessation:
this refers to faculties that are abandoned through the vision of cessation and are abandoned through the dharma-knowledge of cessation.
Regarding those whose causes are abandoned through the vision of cessation while their conditions are abandoned through cultivation:
this refers to faculties that are abandoned through cultivation, which have as their cause the vision of cessation and as their condition abandonment through cultivation.
Regarding those that are abandoned through the vision of cessation but do not have cessation as their object:
this refers to faculties that are abandoned through the vision of cessation but do not have cessation as their object.
Regarding "those abandoned through the vision of cessation, which have no object":
this refers to those roots that lack an object and are abandoned through the vision of cessation.
If a faculty has cessation-through-the-subsequent-knowledge-of-extinction (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*) as its object-condition, does that faculty have cessation-by-seeing-extinction as its cause?

Answer: Those faculties that have cessation-through-the-subsequent-knowledge-of-extinction as their object-condition, those faculties may either have cessation-by-seeing-extinction as their cause or [have other causes].
Either abandoned through the vision of suffering,
or abandoned through the vision of the origin,
or abandoned through cultivation.
Or, due to non-abandonment:

those faculties whose objects are abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*), yet which are themselves abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*).
That is to say:

Those roots abandoned through the vision of cessation that take as their object what is abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of cessation (nirodha-anvaya-jñāna), yet have as their cause what is abandoned through the vision of suffering (duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya): namely, [The following categories apply:]... (as per the original list) ...namely, those factors which are associated with the aforementioned roots and are themselves abandoned through the vision of suffering. These include: the view of self-existence (satkāya-dṛṣṭi), the view of grasping at extremes (antagrāha-dṛṣṭi), the view of false attachment (mithyā-dṛṣṭi), the view of holding to views (dṛṣṭi-parāmarśa), the view of holding to precepts and vows (śīla-vrata-parāmarśa), doubt (vicikitsā), and the afflictions associated with them—namely, greed, hatred, pride, and ignorance—that are abandoned through the vision of suffering. Furthermore, it includes the outflows of desire (kāma-āsrava), the outflows of existence (bhava-āsrava), and the outflows of ignorance (avidyā-āsrava) pertaining to the realm of form (rūpa-dhātu) and the formless realm (ārūpya-dhātu) that are abandoned through the vision of suffering; as well as the fetters, bonds, latent tendencies, floods, yokes, hindrances, and secondary afflictions abandoned through the vision of suffering. It also includes the formations dissociated from mind (citta-viprayukta-saṃskāra) abandoned through the vision of suffering, such as acquisition (prāpti), non-acquisition (aprāpti), the characteristics of conditioned phenomena (saṃskṛta-lakṣaṇa), the name-group (nāma-kāya), the phrase-group (pada-kāya), and the syllable-group (vyañjana-kāya). All such factors are abandoned through the vision of suffering and serve as the causes for those factors abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of cessation that take as their object what is abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of cessation. This concludes the section on those factors abandoned through the vision of suffering that serve as the causes for factors abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of cessation taking as their object what is abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of cessation. What, then, are the factors abandoned through the vision of suffering that serve as the causes for factors abandoned through the vision of suffering taking as their object what is abandoned through the vision of the path (mārga-darśana-prahātavya)? These include: the view of self-existence, the view of grasping at extremes, the view of false attachment, the view of holding to views, the view of holding to precepts and vows, doubt, and the afflictions associated with them—namely, greed, hatred, pride, and ignorance—that are abandoned through the vision of suffering. Furthermore, it includes the outflows of desire, the outflows of existence, and the outflows of ignorance pertaining to the realm of form and the formless realm that are abandoned through the vision of suffering; as well as the fetters, bonds, latent tendencies, floods, yokes, hindrances, and secondary afflictions abandoned through the vision of suffering. What, then, are the factors abandoned through the vision of origination that serve as the causes for factors abandoned through the vision of origination taking as their object what is abandoned through the vision of origination? Roots abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*) have as their object the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna-prahātavya*).

Furthermore, roots abandoned through the vision of origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*) and the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*) have as their cause those abandoned through the vision of suffering and as their object the subsequent knowledge of cessation.
Those that have cessation-subsequent-knowledge (nirodha-anvaya-jñāna) as their object-condition and are abandoned by the vision of the origin (samudaya-darśana-prahātavya) as their cause refer to:
faculties abandoned by the vision of the origin, which have cessation-subsequent-knowledge as their object-condition.

Furthermore, regarding those factors abandoned through the vision of suffering and the vision of cessation, which have as their cause what is abandoned through the vision of origination, and have as their object what is abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of cessation:
those that have as their object what is abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of cessation, while having as their cause what is abandoned through cultivation.
That is to say:

the faculties are abandoned by cultivation, while having the knowledge of the subsequent class regarding cessation (nirodha-anvaya-jñāna) as their object; these have the knowledge of the subsequent class regarding cessation as their object, yet are not caused by that which is not to be abandoned.
That is to say:
the faculty is not abandoned by [the path of] uninterruptedness, but is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*). As it is with cessation; so it is for the others.
It is the same regarding the path (*mārga*).

If various faculties (*indriya*) have their cessation through the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (*duḥkha-dharma-jñāna-prahātavya*), do those faculties have as their object (*ālambana*) that which is to be abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of suffering? Answer:

Those faculties whose cause is abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of suffering (duḥkha-dharma-jñāna-prahātavya) have as their objects either that which is abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of suffering, or that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna-prahātavya),
or that which is abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of origination (samudaya-dharma-jñāna-prahātavya).
Either it takes as its object that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origin,
or that which is abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of cessation,
or that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation.

Some take as their object that which is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma regarding the path; some take as their object that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge regarding the path; some take as their object that which is abandoned by cultivation; and some take as their object that which is not abandoned.
Or there are those that have no object.

Those faculties whose cause is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (*duḥkha-dharma-jñāna*) and which take as their object what is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering are as follows:

The faculties that are abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (duḥkha-dharma-jñāna-prahātavya) have as their object those [dharmas] abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering; and the faculties that are abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of origination (samudaya-dharma-jñāna-prahātavya), which have as their cause those [dharmas] abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering, have as their object those [dharmas] abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering.

Regarding those [factors] abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (*duḥkha-dharma-jñāna-prahātavya*) which take as their object that which is abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna-prahātavya*): it refers to faculties abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of suffering that take as their object that which is abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of suffering;

and to faculties abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of origination (*samudaya-dharma-jñāna-prahātavya*) which have as their cause that which is abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of suffering and take as their object that which is abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of suffering.
Regarding those [factors] abandoned through the dharma-knowledge of suffering that take as their object those abandoned through the dharma-knowledge of origination:
this refers to faculties abandoned through the dharma-knowledge of suffering which take as their object those abandoned through the dharma-knowledge of origination.

Furthermore, regarding those [factors] abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of origin (*samudaya-dharmajñāna*) which have as their cause those abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-dharmajñāna*), and have as their object those abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of origin:
and those which have as their cause those abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of suffering, and have as their object those abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudayānvayajñāna*).
That is to say:

faculties abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (duḥkha-dharma-jñāna), which take as their object that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origination (samudaya-anvaya-jñāna); and faculties abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of origination (samudaya-dharma-jñāna), which have as their cause that which is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering and take as their object that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origination.

Regarding those [factors] abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (*duḥkha-dharmajñāna-prahātavya*) which take as their object that which is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of cessation (*nirodha-dharmajñāna-prahātavya*):
this refers to faculties abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering that take as their object that which is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of cessation.

Furthermore, regarding those [factors] abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of origination and cessation, which are abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering as their cause and abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation as their object;
and those abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering as their cause and abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation as their object.
That is to say:

faculties abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (duḥkha-dharma-jñāna), which take as their object that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation (nirodha-anvaya-jñāna); and faculties abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of origination (samudaya-dharma-jñāna), which have as their cause that which is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering, and take as their object that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation.
Regarding those [factors] abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of suffering which take as their object that which is abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of the path:
this refers to faculties abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of suffering that take as their object that which is abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of the path.

Furthermore, regarding the faculties that are abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of the path (*mārga-dharmajñāna*), they have as their cause those things abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (*duḥkha-dharmajñāna*) and as their object those things abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of the path.

As for those that have as their cause those things abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of suffering and as their object those things abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of the path (*mārgānvayajñāna*): [the same applies].
That is to say:
faculties abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of suffering (duḥkha-dharma-jñāna), which take as their object that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of the path (mārga-anvaya-jñāna);

and faculties abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of origin (samudaya-dharma-jñāna), which have as their cause that which is abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of suffering and take as their object that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of the path.

Regarding those [factors] abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (duḥkha-dharma-jñāna-prahātavya) which take as their object that which is to be abandoned by cultivation (bhāvanā-heya): this refers to faculties (indriya) abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of suffering that take as their object that which is to be abandoned by cultivation.

Furthermore, regarding the faculty of the dharma-knowledge of origin (*samudaya-dharmajñāna*) that is abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*): it has as its cause that which is abandoned through the dharma-knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-dharmajñāna*), and it takes as its object that which is abandoned through cultivation.
Regarding that which has as its cause that which is abandoned through the dharma-knowledge of suffering, and takes as its object that which is not abandoned (*aheya*).
That is to say:

when the faculties are abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of the path, they are caused by what is abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of suffering, and have as their object that which is not abandoned;
or, when they are abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of suffering, they have no object.
That is to say:

there are faculties that do not have [the cessation of suffering] as their object, yet are abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma regarding suffering (*duḥkha-dharma-jñāna*). If a faculty has [the cessation of suffering] as its object and is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma regarding suffering, does that faculty have [the cessation of suffering] as its cause?

Answer: Those faculties that have suffering-dharma-knowledge (duḥkha-dharma-jñāna) as their object and are abandoned by it, those faculties are either abandoned by suffering-dharma-knowledge or abandoned by origin-dharma-knowledge (samudaya-dharma-jñāna).
Either through cultivation for abandonment, or through non-abandonment.
Regarding that which has suffering-dharma-knowledge-abandonment as its object-condition and suffering-dharma-knowledge-abandonment as its cause-condition:
That is to say:

faculties that are abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (duḥkha-dharmajñāna-prahātavya), which take as their object what is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering; and faculties that are abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of origination (samudaya-dharmajñāna-prahātavya), which have as their cause what is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering and take as their object what is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering.
That which is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering as its object, and abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of origination as its cause,
refers to:
faculties abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of origination, which have as their object that which is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering.

Furthermore, those [factors] abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (duḥkha-dharmajñāna-prahātavya) which have as their cause those abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of origination (samudaya-dharmajñāna-prahātavya), have as their object those abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering. Those [factors] abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering which have as their cause those to be abandoned by cultivation (bhāvanā-prahātavya) likewise have as their object those abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering.
That is to say:

when the faculties are abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*), they take as their object that which is abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma regarding suffering (*duḥkha-dharma-jñāna-heya*); yet, while taking as their object that which is abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma regarding suffering, they have non-abandonment (*aheya*) as their cause.
That is to say:
if the faculties are not abandoned by means of the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (*duḥkha-dharma-jñāna*),

but are abandoned by means of the knowledge of the dharma of suffering as their object, then are those faculties which have the knowledge of the subsequent class of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) as their cause also abandoned by means of the knowledge of the subsequent class of suffering as their object?

Answer: Those faculties whose cause is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna) have as their object either that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering,
or that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origin (samudaya-anvaya-jñāna).
Either it takes as its object that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation, or that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of the path,
or that which is abandoned by cultivation.

Or [there are those] that have non-abandonment as their object. Those faculties whose cause is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) and which have what is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering as their object are as follows:
The faculties abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) take as their object those things abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering;

and the faculties abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origination (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*), which have as their cause those things abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering, take as their object those things abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering.

Regarding those [factors] abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) that take as their object those abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of origination (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*):
this refers to faculties abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of suffering that take as their object those abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of origination.

Furthermore, those [factors] abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) which have as their cause those abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*), and take as their object those abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origin;

and those which have as their cause those abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering, and take as their object those abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*).
That is to say:
faculties abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna), which take as their object that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation (nirodha-anvaya-jñāna);

and faculties abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origin (samudaya-anvaya-jñāna) or cessation, which have as their cause that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering and take as their object that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation.

Regarding those [factors] abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) that take as their object what is abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of the path (*mārga-anvaya-jñāna*):
this refers to faculties abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of suffering that take as their object what is abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of the path.

Furthermore, those [factors] abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origin and the subsequent knowledge of the path, which are abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering as their cause, have the subsequent knowledge of the path as their object;
and those abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering as their cause, which are abandoned by cultivation, have the subsequent knowledge of the path as their object.
That is to say:

faculties abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) which take as their object that which is abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*); and faculties abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) or by cultivation, which have as their cause that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering and take as their object that which is abandoned by cultivation.
Regarding those [factors] abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) that take as their object what is not abandoned:

this refers to the faculties abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*) and the subsequent knowledge of the path (*mārga-anvaya-jñāna*), which are abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering and take as their object what is not abandoned.
If a faculty has suffering-subsequent-knowledge-abandonment (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna-prahātavya*) as its object, does that faculty have suffering-subsequent-knowledge-abandonment as its cause?
Answer: Those faculties that have suffering-subsequent-knowledge-abandonment as their object may have suffering-subsequent-knowledge-abandonment as their cause.
Either through the dharma-knowledge of suffering,
or through the dharma-knowledge of origination,
or through the subsequent knowledge of origination.
Either through cultivation and abandonment, or through non-abandonment.
Regarding that which is conditioned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) and has as its cause the subsequent knowledge of suffering:
That is to say:
faculties abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna), which take as their object that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering;

and faculties abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origination (samudaya-anvaya-jñāna), which have as their cause that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering and take as their object that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering.

Regarding those [factors] that have the cessation through subsequent knowledge of suffering as their object-condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*) and the cessation through dharma-knowledge of suffering as their cause-condition (*hetu*):
this refers to faculties (*indriya*) that are abandoned through the dharma-knowledge of suffering and which take the cessation through subsequent knowledge of suffering as their object-condition.

Furthermore, regarding those [factors] abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of origination (*samudaya-dharmajñāna*) that have as their cause those abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (*duḥkha-dharmajñāna*), they have as their object those abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvayajñāna*). Regarding those abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering that have as their cause those abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of origination: [they have as their object those abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origination].
That is to say:

faculties abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of origination (samudaya-dharmajñāna), which have as their object that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (duḥkha-anvayajñāna); and faculties abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of suffering, which have as their cause that which is abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of origination, and which have as their object that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering.

Regarding those [factors] that have the cessation through subsequent knowledge of suffering as their object-condition and the cessation through subsequent knowledge of origination as their cause-condition:

this refers to faculties that are abandoned by the cessation through subsequent knowledge of origination and which have the cessation through subsequent knowledge of suffering as their object-condition.

Furthermore, those [factors] abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) that are roots, which have as their cause the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) and take as their object the subsequent knowledge of suffering,
and those which take as their object the subsequent knowledge of suffering and have as their cause what is to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).
That is to say:

when the faculties are to be abandoned by cultivation, they take as their object that which is to be abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna), while having as their cause that which is not to be abandoned.
That is to say:
the faculty is not abandoned, while its object is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*). As it is with respect to suffering; so it is for the others.
The same applies to the abandonment through the knowledge of the origin (*samudaya-dharma-jñāna*).

Regarding those faculties that have the knowledge of the cessation of phenomena (*nirodha-dharma-jñāna*) as their cause for abandonment, do those faculties have the knowledge of the cessation of phenomena as their object-condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*) for abandonment? Answer:
Those faculties that have the cessation of the knowledge of phenomena (*dharmajñāna*) as their cause for abandonment may, as their object, be abandoned by the cessation of the knowledge of phenomena,
or abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā*),
or abandoned by the unconditioned (*apraheya*).
Or there are those that have no object of perception (*anālambana*).

Those [factors] abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*) that have as their cause those abandoned through the knowledge of the destruction of phenomena (*dharmajñāna-kṣaya*), and which take as their object those abandoned through cultivation, while having as their cause those abandoned through the knowledge of the destruction of phenomena and taking as their object those not to be abandoned (*aheya*).
That is to say:

Those factors abandoned by the knowledge of the cessation of suffering (nirodha-dharma-jñāna) have as their object those not to be abandoned (aheya). Those factors abandoned by the knowledge of the cessation of suffering have no object;
that is to say:

If there is a faculty that does not have [the Truth of] Cessation as its object-condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*), it has the knowledge of the cessation of phenomena (*dharmajñāna*) as its cause-condition (*hetu-pratyaya*). Now, if a faculty has the cessation of phenomena as its object-condition, does that faculty have the knowledge of the cessation of phenomena as its cause-condition? Answer:

Regarding those faculties whose objects are abandoned by the knowledge of the cessation of phenomena (nirodha-dharma-jñāna), those faculties are either abandoned by the knowledge of the cessation of phenomena,
or abandoned by the knowledge of suffering (duḥkha-dharma-jñāna),
or abandoned by the knowledge of origination (samudaya-dharma-jñāna).
Whether through abandonment by cultivation or through non-abandonment,

those faculties that have the knowledge of the cessation of phenomena (*dharmajñāna*) as their object and are abandoned by the knowledge of the cessation of phenomena are [abandoned] through that very cause.
That is to say:

the faculties are abandoned by the knowledge of the cessation of phenomena (*nirodha-dharma-jñāna*), taking as their object that which is abandoned by the knowledge of the cessation of phenomena; and taking as their object that which is abandoned by the knowledge of the cessation of phenomena, they have as their cause that which is abandoned by the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-dharma-jñāna*).
That is to say:

faculties abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (duḥkha-dharma-jñāna-prahātavya), which have as their object that which is abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of cessation (nirodha-dharma-jñāna-prahātavya); and faculties abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of origin (samudaya-dharma-jñāna) or cessation, which have as their cause that which is abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of suffering and have as their object that which is abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of cessation.
Regarding those things that have cessation through the knowledge of the dharma as their object and are abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma regarding origination:
this refers to faculties that are abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma regarding origination and have cessation through the knowledge of the dharma as their object.

Furthermore, regarding those factors abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (*duḥkha-dharmajñāna-prahātavya*) and abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of cessation (*nirodha-dharmajñāna-prahātavya*), which have as their cause that which is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of origination (*samudaya-dharmajñāna-prahātavya*) and as their object that which is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of cessation (*nirodha-dharmajñāna-prahātavya*): [those] which have as their object that which is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of cessation and have as their cause that which is abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).
That is to say:

when the faculties are to be abandoned by cultivation, they take as their object that which is to be abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of cessation; and when taking as their object that which is to be abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of cessation, they have as their cause that which is not to be abandoned.
That is to say:

if the faculties are not abandoned by means of the knowledge of the cessation of phenomena (*dharmajñāna*), but are abandoned by means of the knowledge of the cessation [of suffering] (*nirodhajñāna*), then are those faculties abandoned by means of the subsequent knowledge of the cessation (*anvayajñāna*)? Are those faculties, which have the cessation as their cause and are abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation, also abandoned by means of the subsequent knowledge of cessation?

Answer: Those faculties whose cause is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation (nirodha-anvaya-jñāna) may have as their object that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation,
or they may have as their object that which is not abandoned.

Regarding those faculties that have the knowledge of the destruction of the categories (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*) as their cause for abandonment and take the knowledge of the destruction of the categories as their object:
this refers to faculties abandoned by the knowledge of the destruction of the categories, which take the knowledge of the destruction of the categories as their object.
Regarding those [factors] abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*) which take as their object that which is not to be abandoned:
this refers to faculties abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation that take as their object that which is not to be abandoned.

If a faculty has cessation-through-subsequent-knowledge (nirodha-anvaya-jñāna-bhāvanā-heya) as its object-condition, does that faculty have cessation-through-subsequent-knowledge as its cause? Answer:
Those faculties that have cessation-through-subsequent-knowledge as their object-condition may have cessation-through-subsequent-knowledge as their cause.
Either through the abandonment by means of the dharma-knowledge of suffering,
or through the abandonment by means of the subsequent knowledge of suffering,
or through the abandonment by means of the dharma-knowledge of origination.
Or it may be abandoned through the knowledge of the subsequent class (anvaya-jñāna),
or abandoned through cultivation (bhāvanā-heya), or not abandoned at all.
Regarding those faculties that have cessation-subsequent-knowledge (nirodha-anvaya-jñāna) as their object-condition and are abandoned by cessation-subsequent-knowledge:
this refers to faculties that are abandoned by cessation-subsequent-knowledge and have cessation-subsequent-knowledge as their object-condition.
Regarding those that have cessation-subsequent knowledge (nirodha-anvaya-jñāna) as their object-condition and are abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of suffering (duḥkha-dharma-jñāna):
this refers to faculties (indriya) that are abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of suffering and have cessation-subsequent knowledge as their object-condition.

Furthermore, there are those abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of origin (*samudaya-dharmajñāna*), which have as their cause that abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-dharmajñāna*) and as their object that abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvayajñāna*);
and those abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation, which have as their cause the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvayajñāna*).
That is to say:
faculties abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna) which take as their object that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation (nirodha-anvaya-jñāna);

and faculties abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origin (samudaya-anvaya-jñāna) or cessation, which have as their cause that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering and take as their object that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation.

Regarding those things abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*) which have as their cause those things abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of origin (*samudaya-dharma-jñāna*):
this refers to faculties abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of origin that take as their object those things abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation.

Furthermore, there are faculties that are abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-dharma-jñāna*), have the origin as their cause (*hetu*) through the dharma-knowledge of origin (*samudaya-dharma-jñāna*), and have cessation as their object (*ālambana*) through the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*).

There are also those that have cessation as their object through the subsequent knowledge of cessation and have the origin as their cause through the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*).
That is to say:

those faculties abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origination (samudaya-anvaya-jñāna) which take as their object that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation (nirodha-anvaya-jñāna); and those faculties abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna) or the subsequent knowledge of cessation, which have as their cause that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origination and take as their object that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation.
Regarding those conditioned by the cessation through subsequent knowledge (*anvaya-jñāna*) and having cultivation as their cause:
this refers to faculties that are abandoned through cultivation and which take as their object the cessation through subsequent knowledge.
That which has cessation through subsequent knowledge as its object-condition but is not abandoned by its cause refers to:
faculties that are not abandoned, yet have cessation through subsequent knowledge as their object-condition.
As it is with cessation,

so it is with the path. Regarding those faculties whose cause is abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (*duḥkha-dharma-jñāna-prahātavya*), are those faculties conditioned by what is abandoned through the vision of suffering (*darśana-duḥkha-prahātavya*)?

Answer: Those faculties whose causes are abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (duḥkha-dharma-jñāna) have as their objects either that which is abandoned through the vision of suffering (duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya) or that which is abandoned through the vision of origination (samudaya-darśana-prahātavya).

Some take as their object that which is abandoned through the vision of cessation; some take as their object that which is abandoned through the vision of the path; and some take as their object that which is abandoned through cultivation.
Some have non-abandonment as their object;
some have no object at all.

These faculties, which have the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (*duḥkha-dharma-jñāna*) as their cause, have that which is abandoned through the vision of suffering (*darśana-duḥkha-prahātavya*) as their object.
That is to say:

faculties abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (duḥkha-dharma-jñāna), which take as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of suffering (duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya); and faculties abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of origination (samudaya-dharma-jñāna), which have as their cause that which is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering, and take as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of suffering.

Those abandoned through the dharma-knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-dharmajñāna-prahātavya*) which take as their object that which is to be abandoned through the vision of origination (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*):
this refers to faculties abandoned through the dharma-knowledge of suffering that take as their object that which is to be abandoned through the vision of origination.

Furthermore, those [factors] abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of origination (*samudaya-dharmajñāna*) which have as their cause those abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (*duḥkha-dharmajñāna*), and which take as their object those abandoned by the vision of origination (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*); and those which have as their cause those abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering, and which take as their object those abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*).
That is to say:

faculties abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (duḥkha-dharma-jñāna), which have as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of cessation (nirodha-darśana-prahātavya); and faculties abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of origin (samudaya) or cessation, which have as their cause that which is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering, and have as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of cessation.

Regarding those [factors] abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (duḥkha-dharma-jñāna-prahātavya) that take as their object what is abandoned through the vision of the path (darśana-mārga):
this refers to faculties (indriya) abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of suffering which take as their object what is abandoned through the vision of the path.

Furthermore, regarding the faculties (*indriya*), the knowledge of the dharma of origination (*samudaya-dharmajñāna*), and the knowledge of the dharma of the path (*mārga-dharmajñāna*) that are abandoned through abandonment, they have as their cause that which is abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (*duḥkha-dharmajñāna*), and as their object, that which is abandoned through seeing the path (*darśanamārga*). As for those abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma of suffering that have as their object that which is abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*): [the same applies].
That is to say:

faculties abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (duḥkha-dharma-jñāna) which take as their object that which is abandoned by cultivation (bhāvanā-heya); and faculties abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of origin (samudaya-dharma-jñāna) and abandoned by cultivation, which have as their cause that which is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering and take as their object that which is abandoned by cultivation.

Regarding those [factors] abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (*duḥkha-dharmajñāna-prahātavya*) which take as their object that which is not to be abandoned (*aprahātavyālambana*): this refers to the faculties (*indriya*) abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of cessation (*nirodha-dharmajñāna*) and the knowledge of the dharma of the path (*mārga-dharmajñāna*), which are themselves abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering and take as their object that which is not to be abandoned.
Regarding those abandoned through the dharma-knowledge of suffering that have no object:
this refers to the root of non-apprehension, which is abandoned through the dharma-knowledge of suffering.

If a faculty has as its object that which is abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), is that faculty caused by the knowledge of the dharma regarding suffering (*duḥkha-dharma-jñāna-prahātavya*)? Answer:
Those faculties that have as their object that which is abandoned through the vision of suffering may, in some cases, be caused by the knowledge of the dharma regarding suffering.
Either through the subsequent knowledge of suffering,
or through the dharma-knowledge of origin,
or through the subsequent knowledge of origin.
Whether through cultivation and abandonment, or through non-abandonment:
those faculties whose objects are abandoned by the vision of suffering, and which are abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering; [these are so defined].
That is to say:

the faculties that are abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (duḥkha-dharma-jñāna), which take as their object what is abandoned by the vision of suffering (duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya); and the faculties that are abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of origination (samudaya-dharma-jñāna), which have as their cause what is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering, and which take as their object what is abandoned by the vision of suffering.

Regarding those [factors] that have as their object what is abandoned by the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), yet are themselves abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*):
this refers to faculties (*indriya*) that are abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering, which take as their object what is abandoned by the vision of suffering.

Furthermore, regarding those [factors] abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) which have as their cause those abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*), and which take as their object those abandoned by the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*):
there are those that take as their object those abandoned by the vision of suffering, while having as their cause those abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of origin (*samudaya-dharma-jñāna*).
That is to say:

faculties abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of origination (samudaya-dharmajñāna), which take as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of suffering (duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya); and faculties abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (duḥkha-dharmajñāna), which have as their cause that which is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of origination, and take as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of suffering.

Regarding those [factors] that have the cessation through seeing suffering as their object-condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*) and the knowledge of the category of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) as their causal-condition (*hetu*):
this refers to faculties that are abandoned by the knowledge of the category of origin and which have the cessation through seeing suffering as their object-condition.

Furthermore, regarding those [factors] abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) that are roots, which have as their cause the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) and as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of suffering (*darśana-duḥkha-heya*), and which have as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of suffering and as their cause that which is abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*):
it refers to—
Those factors abandoned through cultivation that take as their object those factors abandoned through seeing suffering,
yet have as their cause those factors not to be abandoned:
this refers to—
If the faculties are not abandoned by the path of seeing suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*),

but are abandoned by the path of seeing [the origin], are those faculties whose causes are abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) also abandoned by the path of seeing suffering? Answer:

Those faculties whose cause is to be abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna) have as their objects either that which is to be abandoned by the vision of suffering (duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya),
or that which is to be abandoned by the vision of origination (samudaya-darśana-prahātavya), or that which is to be abandoned by the vision of cessation (nirodha-darśana-prahātavya).

Some take as their object that which is abandoned by the path of seeing; some take as their object that which is abandoned by the path of cultivation; and some take as their object that which is not abandoned.

Regarding those faculties whose cause is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) and which take as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of suffering (*darśana-duḥkha-heya*):
this refers to faculties abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering, which take as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of suffering.

Furthermore, regarding those [factors] abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) which have as their cause those abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*), and which take as their object those abandoned by seeing suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*):
those which have as their cause those abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering, and which take as their object those abandoned by seeing origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*).
That is to say:

faculties abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna), which take as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of origination (samudaya-darśana-prahātavya); and faculties abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origination (samudaya-anvaya-jñāna), which have as their cause that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering and take as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of origination.

Regarding those [factors] abandoned through subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna-prahātavya*) that take as their object what is abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*):
this refers to faculties abandoned through subsequent knowledge of suffering that take as their object what is abandoned through the vision of cessation.

Furthermore, those [factors] abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origination and cessation, which have as their cause those abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering, and take as their object those abandoned by the vision of cessation;
and those abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering, which take as their object those abandoned by the vision of the path.
That is to say:

faculties abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna) that take as their object what is abandoned by the vision of the path (mārga-darśana-prahātavya); and faculties abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origin (samudaya-anvaya-jñāna) or the subsequent knowledge of the path (mārga-anvaya-jñāna) that take as their object what is abandoned by the vision of the path.
Regarding those [factors] abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) which take as their object those abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*):
this refers to faculties abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering that take as their object those abandoned through cultivation.

Furthermore, those [factors] abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) and abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*), which have as their cause those abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*), take as their object those abandoned by cultivation.
Those which have as their cause those abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering take as their object those that are not abandoned (*aheya*).
That is to say:

a faculty that is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of the path (*mārgānvayajñāna*) has as its cause that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkhānvayajñāna*), while its object is not abandoned.
Suppose a faculty has as its object that which is abandoned by the vision of suffering (*duḥkhadarśana*); is that faculty caused by the subsequent knowledge of suffering?

Answer: Those faculties that have as their object what is abandoned through the vision of suffering (duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya) are themselves either abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of suffering (duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna) or abandoned through the dharma-knowledge of suffering (duḥkha-dharma-jñāna).
Either abandoned through the knowledge of the origin (samudaya-dharma-jñāna), or abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of the origin (samudaya-anvaya-jñāna),
or abandoned through cultivation (bhāvanā-heya).
Or, due to non-abandonment:

those faculties whose objects are abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), yet which are themselves abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkhe ’nvaya-jñāna-prahātavya*).
That is to say:

Those faculties abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) that take as their object what is abandoned by the vision of suffering (*darśana-duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*); and those faculties abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) which have as their cause what is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering and take as their object what is abandoned by the vision of suffering;
and those which take as their object what is abandoned by the vision of suffering and have as their cause what is abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-dharma-jñāna*).
That is to say:
faculties abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (duḥkha-dharma-jñāna), which take as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of suffering;

and faculties abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of origination (samudaya-dharma-jñāna), which have as their cause that which is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering and take as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of suffering.
Regarding those things that have the cessation through seeing suffering as their object-condition and the knowledge of the dharma regarding the origin as their cause:
this refers to faculties that have the knowledge of the dharma regarding the origin as their cause and have the cessation through seeing suffering as their object-condition.

Furthermore, regarding those [factors] that are abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (*duḥkha-dharmajñāna*) with respect to their roots, which are abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of origination (*samudaya-dharmajñāna*) as their cause and abandoned by the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana*) as their object; and those abandoned by the vision of suffering as their object, which are abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origination (*samudaya-anvayajñāna*) as their cause.
That is to say:

faculties abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origination (samudaya-anvaya-jñāna), which take as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of suffering (duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya); and faculties abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna), which have as their cause that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origination and take as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of suffering.

Regarding those [factors] that have as their object what is abandoned through the vision of suffering (duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya), yet have as their cause what is abandoned through cultivation (bhāvanā-prahātavya): this refers to faculties (indriya) that are abandoned through cultivation, which take as their object what is abandoned through the vision of suffering.
That which has as its object that which is abandoned by seeing suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), but whose cause is not abandoned,
refers to:
faculties that are not abandoned, which have as their object that which is abandoned by seeing suffering.
As it is regarding suffering,
so it is regarding the origin.

If those faculties have their cause abandoned through the knowledge of the destruction of phenomena (*nirodha-dharma-jñāna*), do those faculties have as their object that which is abandoned through the vision of the destruction (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*)?

Answer: Those faculties whose causes are abandoned by the knowledge of the cessation of phenomena (nirodha-dharma-jñāna) may have as their objects those things abandoned by the vision of cessation (nirodha-darśana-prahātavya), or they may have as their objects those things abandoned by cultivation (bhāvanā-prahātavya).
Some have non-abandonment as their object; some have no object.
There are those faculties whose cause is abandoned by the knowledge of the cessation of phenomena (dharmajñāna), while their object is abandoned by the vision of cessation (nirodhadarśana).
That is to say:

those faculties that are abandoned by the knowledge of the cessation of phenomena (dharmajñāna), taking as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of cessation (nirodhadarśana); and those that are abandoned by the knowledge of the cessation of phenomena, taking as their object that which is abandoned by cultivation (bhāvanā).
That is to say:

when the faculties are abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*), they have as their cause that which is abandoned through the knowledge of the destruction of phenomena (*dharmajñāna-kṣaya*), and they take as their object that which is abandoned through cultivation; or, when they have as their cause that which is abandoned through the knowledge of the destruction of phenomena, they take as their object that which is not abandoned (*aheya*).
That is to say:

those factors abandoned by the knowledge of the cessation of the truths (nirodha-dharma-jñāna) which have as their object that which is not to be abandoned (aheya), and those which have no object at all, are abandoned by the knowledge of the cessation of the truths.
That is to say:

there are faculties that do not take [the cessation of suffering] as their object, yet have the knowledge of the destruction of phenomena (*dharmajñāna*) as their cause for abandonment. Now, if a faculty takes the cessation of suffering as its object and is abandoned by the knowledge of the cessation of phenomena, does that faculty have the knowledge of the destruction of phenomena as its cause for abandonment?
Answer: Those faculties that have as their object the cessation through seeing (*darśana-prahātavya*) are either abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma regarding cessation (*nirodha-dharma-jñāna*),
or they are abandoned by the subsequent knowledge regarding cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*).
Either through the abandonment by means of the dharma-knowledge of suffering,
or through the abandonment by means of the subsequent knowledge of suffering,
or through the abandonment by means of the dharma-knowledge of origin.
Or they are abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of the origin;
or they are abandoned through cultivation;
or they are not abandoned.
Regarding those faculties that have cessation through seeing as their object and are abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of cessation:
this refers to faculties abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of cessation which take as their object that which is abandoned through seeing cessation.
Regarding those [factors] that have cessation through seeing as their object-condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*) and are abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*):
this refers to faculties (*indriya*) that are abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation and which have cessation through seeing as their object-condition.
Regarding those [factors] that have cessation through seeing as their object-condition (*ālambana*) and are abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (*duḥkha-dharma-jñāna*):
this refers to faculties (*indriya*) that are abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering and have cessation through seeing as their object-condition.

Furthermore, regarding those [factors] abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of cessation (*nirodha-dharmajñāna*) within the roots of origination (*samudaya*), which are abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (*duḥkha-dharmajñāna*) as their cause and abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodhadarśana*) as their object:
those abandoned by the vision of cessation as their object and abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkhānvayajñāna*) as their cause.
That is to say:

faculties abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna) which take as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of cessation (nirodha-darśana-prahātavya); and faculties abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origin (samudaya-anvaya-jñāna) or cessation (nirodha-anvaya-jñāna), which have as their cause that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering and take as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of cessation.
Regarding those [factors] that have cessation through seeing as their object-condition and are abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of origin:
this refers to faculties that are abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of origin and have cessation through seeing as their object-condition.

Furthermore, regarding those [factors] abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering and cessation, which have as their cause those abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of origination, and as their object those abandoned by the vision of cessation:
those that have as their object those abandoned by the vision of cessation, and have as their cause those abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origination.
That is to say:

faculties abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origination (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) which take as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*); and faculties abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) or the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*), which have as their cause that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origination and take as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of cessation.
Regarding those that have cessation through seeing as their object-condition and cultivation as their cause:
this refers to faculties that are abandoned through cultivation, which take cessation through seeing as their object-condition.
Regarding that which is conditioned by the vision of the cessation [of suffering] and has non-abandonment as its cause:
this refers to faculties that are not abandoned and are conditioned by the vision of the cessation [of suffering].

If the various faculties have cessation-subsequent-knowledge (nirodha-anvaya-jñāna) as their cause for abandonment, do those faculties have cessation-seeing (nirodha-darśana) as their object for abandonment? Answer:
Those faculties that have cessation-subsequent-knowledge as their cause for abandonment may have cessation-seeing as their object for abandonment.
Or [there are those] that take non-abandonment as their object.

Those faculties whose cause is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*) and which take what is abandoned by the vision of cessation (*darśana-nirodha-prahātavya*) as their object are as follows:

Those whose roots are abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*) and which take as their object that which is abandoned through the vision of cessation (*darśana-nirodha-prahātavya*). Those whose roots are abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of cessation and which do not take as their object that which is abandoned [by the paths of vision] are as follows:

If a faculty is abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*) and has as its object that which is not to be abandoned (*aprahātavya*), is that faculty caused by the subsequent knowledge of cessation? Answer: [The faculty] is abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of cessation, and it has as its object that which is not to be abandoned. Suppose a faculty has as its object that which is to be abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*); is that faculty caused by the subsequent knowledge of cessation?
Answer: [It may be.]

Regarding those faculties that have as their object that which is abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodhadarśana-prahātavya*), those faculties are either abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodhānvaya-jñāna*),
or abandoned through the dharma-knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-dharma-jñāna*), or abandoned through the dharma-knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-dharma-jñāna*).
Either through the subsequent knowledge of suffering,
or through the dharma-knowledge of origin,
or through the subsequent knowledge of origin.
Or they are abandoned through cultivation, or not abandoned at all.

As for those faculties whose objects are to be abandoned by the vision of cessation and which are abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodhānvayajñāna*): [they are abandoned through cultivation].
That is to say:

when the faculties are abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*), they take as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of cessation (*darśana-nirodha-heya*); and when taking as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of cessation, they have as their cause that which is abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-dharma-jñāna*).
That is to say:

the faculties that are abandoned by the knowledge of the cessation of phenomena (dharmajñāna) take as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of cessation (nirodhadarśana), while being caused by that which is abandoned by the knowledge of suffering (duḥkhadharmajñāna).
That is to say:

faculties abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (duḥkha-dharma-jñāna), which have as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of cessation (nirodha-darśana-prahātavya); and faculties abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of origination (samudaya) and cessation, which have as their cause that which is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering, and have as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of cessation.
Regarding those [factors] that have cessation through seeing as their object-condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*) and are abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*):
this refers to faculties that are abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering and which have cessation through seeing as their object-condition.

Furthermore, those [factors] abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) and abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*), which have as their cause those abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*), and which take as their object those abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*);
and those which take as their object those abandoned by the vision of cessation, and have as their cause those abandoned by the dharma-knowledge of origin (*samudaya-dharma-jñāna*).
That is to say:
